title: Paint House IV
summary: Given an even number of houses in a line and a cost matrix for painting each house with one of three colors, find the minimum cost to paint the houses ensuring no two adjacent houses have the same color and houses equidistant from the ends are also differently colored.
statement: Given an even number of houses in a line and a cost matrix for painting each house with one of three colors, find the minimum cost to paint the houses ensuring no two adjacent houses have the same color and houses equidistant from the ends are also differently colored.
constraints: n is even, 2 <= n <= 100,000, and cost has n rows of three nonnegative painting costs.
Adjacent houses must use different colors.
Each mirrored pair i and n-1-i must also use different colors; return the minimum total cost.
hints: Process houses as mirrored pairs so both long-range and adjacent restrictions stay local.
Keep the previous left and right colors as a nine-state dynamic program.
For each inward pair choose distinct colors that also differ from their same-side predecessor, then add both costs.
The state records exactly the colors that can constrain the next pair, so optimal substructure holds.
editorial: The state records exactly the colors that can constrain the next pair, so optimal substructure holds.

tests.explanation: Colors [1,2,3,2] cost three plus two plus one plus three, totaling nine.
The two adjacent and mirrored houses use colors one and two for total cost three.
